title: Cerberus: Terraform observability module — collector lifecycle, log-shipping, and health‑orchestration
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Replace the ad-hoc observability IaC pieces in VPC deployments with a single opinionated Terraform module (codename: Cerberus) that manages Prometheus/Grafana, the OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel), and log shippers (Fluent Bit / Vector) and provides resilient upgrade and health orchestration.

Scope:
- Author a reusable TF module that instantiates: Prometheus (remote-write configured), Grafana (provisioned dashboards + datasource), OTel collector (receiver/processor/exporter config templated), and a configurable log-forwarder.
- Provide lifecycle hooks and health probes so the orchestration layer (cell-reconciler) can safely roll upgrades and detect partial failures.
- Implement canary upgrade flow (N% of cells), automated rollback criteria based on health signals and SLO regressions, and a remediation path (restart/replace) for unhealthy collector instances.
- Ensure minimal blast radius: support toggling individual components (metrics only / logs only / full stack) and optional managed vs. self-hosted Grafana.
- Strong IaC hygiene: remote state locking, deterministic module inputs, idempotent migrations, and CI plans in PRs.

Non-goals: migrating existing legacy observability stacks in customer VPCs in this ticket; that will be follow-ups after module stabilization.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes a Terraform registry-compatible interface with documented inputs/outputs
A dry-run canary upgrade can be executed in a staging cell and rolled back via the module output flags
Health endpoints exposed: /healthz and /ready for OTel collector and log-forwarder, and Prometheus target status validated in Grafana dashboard
CI pipeline runs terraform fmt/validate/plan and blocks PRs with drift or destructive changes unless explicitly approved
Automated canary metrics (error rate, export latency, OTel internal metrics) are captured and trigger rollback when thresholds exceeded
terraform_changes: New module: modules/cerberus-observability with submodules: prometheus, grafana, otel_collector, log_forwarder
Inputs: network_ids, subnet_ids, iam_role_arns, storage_bucket, enable_grafana, retention_days, canary_percent
State: separate remote state per environment with locking and versioned state migration script
Upgrade hooks: pre_upgrade_plan, post_upgrade_probe (retries/backoff), canary_split configuration
rollout_plan: 1) Merge TF module into infra main branch behind feature flag
2) Run CI plan in staging cell and validate dashboards + /healthz endpoints
3) Deploy canary to 10% of cells; run 24h smoke harness capturing OTel internal metrics
4) If metrics stable, promote to 50% for 6h, then 100% with delayed finalizer
5) If rollback criteria met at any stage, run automated rollback and create incident with collector logs attached

2025-03-11 Ravi Patel: Spike complete — validated OTel config templating approach. Found that the collector config needs templated exporter blocks per-tenant; added design note in Confluence.

2025-03-13 Ravi Patel: Prototyped canary gating using error_rate and export_latency derived from otel_collector_processor_metrics. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/7123

2025-03-14 Avery Chen: Added CI plan job that runs terraform plan with approval gate and automatic drift detection. Linking Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cerberus-Observability-Module
risks_mitigations: Risk: OTel config changes can silently drop spans/metrics. Mitigation: Add pre-flight config linter and end-to-end benchmark in staging.
Risk: Terraform destroy or drift during upgrade. Mitigation: plan-only runs in CI and require manual approval for destructive plans; keep backups of PVs and buckets.
Risk: Increased network egress from remote-write. Mitigation: add sampling and batching config defaults; surface cost in module outputs
